security_audit.summary: The audit confirms low-severity network dependencies for p5.js and Google Fonts in the template and example instructions. All static external-command, script-execution, and reconnaissance findings are false positives from markdown fences, ordinary wording, or a JavaScript regex match.

remediation.issue: The viewer template loads p5.js and Google Fonts from external URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Document this network behavior clearly, or vendor trusted local copies for offline and privacy-sensitive use.

remediation.issue: Remote script loading lacks integrity metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Add Subresource Integrity and crossorigin attributes when keeping CDN-hosted JavaScript dependencies.

content.value_statement: Generative art requests often need structure, reproducibility, and usable controls. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create original p5.js artwork with seeded variation.
actual_capabilities: Creates an algorithmic philosophy before implementation to guide the visual system.
Builds p5.js generative art with deterministic seed controls.
Uses a provided HTML viewer template with sidebar controls and canvas layout.
Defines tunable parameters for particles, flow fields, colors, and other visual systems.
Produces self-contained HTML artifacts that run in a browser with p5.js loaded from a CDN.
Supports exploration through previous, next, random, and direct seed entry controls.
limitations: Generated artifacts rely on external CDN resources unless the author vendors dependencies locally.
The skill provides templates and guidance, not a complete finished artwork by itself.
Browser performance depends on particle counts, canvas size, and device capability.
It avoids copying living artists or copyrighted styles and focuses on original algorithms.

use_cases.title: Prototype Generative Art Concepts
use_cases.description: Turn a visual idea into a reproducible p5.js sketch with parameters and seed navigation.

use_cases.title: Create Interactive Design Studies
use_cases.description: Generate browser-based visual studies that stakeholders can adjust without editing code.

use_cases.title: Teach Computational Aesthetics
use_cases.description: Show how noise, particles, fields, and deterministic randomness shape visual outcomes.

prompt_templates.title: Begin a Simple Artwork
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when you have a basic visual direction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a p5.js generative artwork about flowing light. Include a short algorithmic philosophy, seed controls, and three simple parameters.

prompt_templates.title: Explore a Visual System
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when you want a richer interactive study.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an interactive algorithmic art artifact based on particle motion and field forces. Make the parameters meaningful and explain the seed behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an Existing Concept
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when a concept needs better structure or controls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this generative art idea into a clear algorithmic philosophy and p5.js viewer. Keep the output original and avoid copying artist styles.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Gallery-Ready Artifact
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a polished advanced result.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a polished self-contained p5.js artwork with deterministic seeds, tuned parameters, elegant controls, and a distinctive computational philosophy.

output_examples.input: Create generative art inspired by tidal motion and quiet geometry.
output_examples.output: A named algorithmic philosophy, followed by an interactive p5.js artifact with wave fields, seed navigation, and adjustable flow density.

output_examples.input: Make a particle system that feels like controlled chaos.
output_examples.output: A browser-ready artwork with thousands of seeded particles, tunable turbulence, color controls, and a reset workflow.

output_examples.input: Generate 100 visual variations from one algorithm.
output_examples.output: A single viewer that lets users move through numbered seeds and compare deterministic variations from the same system.

best_practices: Start from the provided viewer template so seed controls and layout remain consistent.
Define parameters from the artwork concept, not from a generic effects list.
Use seeded randomness for every random and noise decision that affects the artwork.
anti_patterns: Do not copy a named artist or reproduce a copyrighted visual style.
Do not create static images when the request needs an algorithmic system.
Do not add high particle counts without checking browser performance.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates original p5.js generative art concepts and browser-ready interactive artifacts.

faq.question: Does it support reproducible outputs?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions require seeded randomness so the same seed can recreate the same result.

faq.question: Can users adjust the artwork?
faq.answer: Yes. The template includes parameter controls, color controls, and seed navigation.

faq.question: Does the HTML run offline?
faq.answer: Not by default. The template loads p5.js and fonts from external web resources.

faq.question: Can it copy a specific artist style?
faq.answer: No. The skill instructs the model to create original algorithmic art and avoid copying existing artists.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
